key_insight: SpatialEvo uses deterministic, procedurally controlled 3D environments to produce reliable ground-truth signals for self-training, avoiding the consensus-based pseudo-label loop that amplifies a model's own spatial errors.
problem_solved: Alleviates dependence on expensive geometric annotations and prevents self-supervised training from reinforcing model mistakes when learning 3D spatial reasoning.
method: Create deterministic geometric environments that yield exact, reproducible ground-truth geometry and spatial relations.
Run a self-evolving training loop where the model interacts with the environment to collect labeled experiences and iteratively correct its errors.
Apply curriculum and controlled perturbations to expose failure modes and prevent error reinforcement, enabling continuous improvement without human labels.
impact: Provides a scalable, low-cost path to continually improve 3D spatial reasoning models, boosting robustness and generalization for embodied AI, robotics, and 3D perception systems.
visual_elements: Schematic of a deterministic 3D environment with agent and overlaid ground-truth geometry/relations
Flowchart of the self-evolving loop: model → environment → labeled experience → model update (iterative cycle)

Before/after scene visual: predicted spatial relations vs ground-truth to illustrate corrected errors
paper_title: SpatialEvo: Self-Evolving Spatial Intelligence via Deterministic Geometric Environments
paper_authors: Dinging Li, Yingxiu Zhao, Xinrui Cheng, Kangheng Lin, Hongbo Peng
